thread.title: Trump-backed candidates win closely watched Arizona primary races
thread.title_full: Trump-backed candidates win closely watched Arizona primary races

author: KSLcom
title: Trump-backed candidates win closely watched Arizona primary races
text:
Tuesday's Arizona primaries saw conservative Republican candidates and moderate Democratic candidates nominated for high-profile races for governor and a U.S. House seat.
Supporters cheer during a "Get Out the Vote" rally in support of U.S. representative and Republican candidate for Arizona governor Andy Biggs on the last day of early voting in Gilbert, Ariz.
, Friday. Biggs easily won the primary election on Tuesday. Rep. Andy Biggs will face Democratic Gov.
Katie Hobbs in the November gubernatorial race. Arizona's 1st Congressional District is a key target as Democrats look to retake control of the House of Representatives. SCOTTSDALE, Ariz. — Republican voters in Tuesday's Arizona primaries nominated conservative candidates for high-profile races for governor and a U.S. House seat, as Democrats rallied behind moderates leading up to the Nov. 3 midterm elections.
The results also marked wins for President Donald Trump, who endorsed victorious Republicans in two of the most-watched primary races. Rep. Andy Biggs comfortably won the Republican nomination for governor and will face Democratic Gov. Katie Hobbs, who was unopposed in her primary.
With Trump's endorsement in hand, Biggs handily defeated Rep. David Schweikert and two other candidates, according to media projections. Biggs is a former head of the House Freedom Caucus, which advocates deep cuts to social safety net programs as part of its platform of addressing federal budget deficits and debt. In 2022, Republicans similarly nominated a candidate for governor, Kari Lake, who ended up being defeated by Hobbs in a close race.
Meanwhile, former professional football player Jay Feely, who is also backed by Trump, defeated two challengers and secured the Republican nomination that puts him on the November ballot for election to Arizona's 1st Congressional District. Democrats have targeted this open Phoenix metropolitan district seat as a top priority in their quest to win back majority control of the House from Republicans.
Registered Republicans outnumber registered Democrats in Arizona, but the large number of independents makes for a state that is considered closely divided. Trump congratulated his allies' victories in a social media post on Wednesday.
"A complete sweep," he wrote in all capital letters. With 96% of votes counted as of Wednesday morning, Amish Shah was leading Marlene Galan-Woods, 40.5%-33.6%. Shah, an emergency room doctor, narrowly defeated Galan-Woods for the party nomination in 2024. She is a former Republican and ex-broadcast journalist whose supporters range from Sen.
Mark Kelly, an Arizona Democrat, to the Democratic Congressional Campaign Committee. Republicans currently hold 218 House seats to Democrats' 212 seats, not counting one independent who caucuses with Republicans and four vacancies. Democrats need a net gain of four seats to regain majority control of the House starting in 2027. Political analysts see the November race as a toss-up in a district that Democratic presidential candidate Joe Biden won in 2020.
Trump won the district in 2024. A second House seat is also considered a November toss-up in the 6th Congressional District, currently held by Republican Rep. Juan Ciscomani. Ciscomani had no primary challenger, and neither did Democratic candidate JoAnna Mendoza.
The governor's race between Hobbs and Biggs is expected to be hard-fought. However, the Cook Political Report has adjusted its forecast from a toss-up to "lean Democratic," noting that Biggs is a 2020 presidential election denier and a "potentially polarizing" figure in this swing state.
That is a narrative that Democrats hope also carries them to victory in the race for the governorship, as well as three of the nine House races in Arizona this autumn, including the 2nd District seat currently held by Republican Rep. Eli Crane. Media outlets have reported that Cindy McCain, the widow of the late maverick Republican Sen. John McCain, has endorsed Hobbs in her race against Biggs.
During Trump's first term as president he engaged in attacks on McCain, including over his 2017 vote against dismantling the "Obamacare" health insurance law also known as the Affordable Care Act. The November elections, coming midway into Trump's second term, will determine whether his fellow Republicans will continue to control both chambers of Congress through 2028, or whether Democrats will put up roadblocks to his administration by winning majorities in the House of Representatives, Senate or both.
